html.rich.privacy.cloudflare.1: The game is hosted on Cloudflare Pages. Like any web server, Cloudflare receives your IP address and technical browser data to serve the page.
html.rich.privacy.cloudflare.2: Cloudflare Web Analytics counts visits and measures loading speed in aggregate, without cookies or identifiers to track you. It doesn’t receive your games or scores. If a blocker stops it, the game still works.
html.rich.privacy.device.1: Your browser stores your personal bests and game preferences, such as sync, menu sound, graphics quality, whether you’ve done the practice and which notices you’ve seen. It also stores your stats (games, time in the square, hits, misses by type, streaks and the days you play), separately for each profile; deleting a profile also deletes its stats. They stay on your device, apart from the totals sent to your profile if you have one (see below), and are deleted if you clear this site’s data in your browser. We don’t use tracking or advertising cookies: the data the game stores on your device is essential for the features you’ve requested, so we don’t ask for cookie consent.
html.rich.privacy.leaderboards.1: Viewing leaderboards doesn’t create a profile. Posting a score is optional: the game and your device’s personal bests work just the same without posting.
html.rich.privacy.leaderboards.2: Posting creates an anonymous profile, without a password, on Supabase (servers in Frankfurt, EU). Once you post with a nickname, your later results are uploaded too. You can turn this off in Settings. It stores your nickname and your best result for each figure and level per season (hits, points, streak and date). Your nickname and results are public: use a nickname, not your real name. Like any server, Supabase also receives the connection’s IP address.
html.rich.privacy.leaderboards.3: When you create your profile (the first time you post a result) or ask for a code by email, Cloudflare Turnstile also checks that you’re not a robot. Usually you won’t see anything; sometimes it asks you to tick a box. To do this, Cloudflare processes technical connection and browser signals (IP address, browser and its settings) solely to stop bots, not to track you or for advertising. If the check can’t run, the game still works.
html.rich.privacy.leaderboards.4: Your browser remembers your profile session and nickname so you can post again. A nickname is unique. Without a confirmed email, it’s a guest profile and only lives in this browser. If you clear its data, the profile is lost and can’t be recovered. If a guest profile goes 30 days without playing, someone else can take its nickname; its results stay. With a confirmed email, the nickname is yours and the profile is kept until you delete it: you can do this at any time via the Profile button (Delete profile).
html.rich.privacy.leaderboards.5: Stats. If you have a profile, the game sends it your total stats across all your devices (games, time in the square, hits, GUAPA, balloons, HOLD notes, falls, streaks and stars) and the days you’ve played, as dates only. Totals are public: anyone tapping your nickname on a leaderboard can see them. Days are private: only you can see them, in your Profile. The time you play and device data are never sent (the device is represented by a random number that never leaves the server). Everything is deleted with the profile.
html.rich.privacy.leaderboards.6: Email (optional). If you confirm an email on your profile (Profile button), we store it in Supabase so you don’t lose your profile and can receive a 6-digit code to recover it; Resend delivers the code (a US company with a server in Ireland, EU). Your address never appears on the leaderboard: only an “Email confirmed” badge appears beside your nickname. An email entered but not confirmed doesn’t count and is deleted with the profile. If the email belongs to another profile, the code signs you into that profile: this browser’s profile and its results aren’t added. We don’t use it for anything else or send you advertising. Legal basis: your consent when you enter it and the code. If you’re under 14, ask an adult first.
html.rich.privacy.share.1: The image and challenge link are created on your device. The game doesn’t send them anywhere: you only share what you choose, using the app you choose, and that app applies its own privacy policy.
html.rich.privacy.share.2: The challenge link only contains the hit percentage and level (for example, ?repte=94-2), with no identifier. If you have a nickname, it appears on the image; you can remove it using “Include my nickname”. Your browser remembers the image format you chose.
html.rich.privacy.share.3: “Share image” sends only the image, with no text. WhatsApp, X and “More” send only the text and link; where there’s no share menu, “Copy” puts the text and link on your device’s clipboard.
html.rich.privacy.errors.1: If the game fails, it sends an anonymous report to Sentry (Functional Software, Inc.), which stores the data in the EU (Germany). It is only used to find and fix errors.
html.rich.privacy.errors.2: The report contains the error message, code trace, browser and device type, and game state (screen, level, graphics quality). It does not store your IP address, use cookies, include nicknames or results, or record your screen.
html.rich.privacy.feedback.1: You need a profile with a confirmed email address to write from the game. If you write to the Square mailbox, offer materials or get in touch as a colla or organisation, a small Cloudflare service sends your message, your confirmed email address, the options you selected and, if provided, the organisation's name to the project's mailbox, along with the game version and browser type. We use this to read your message and reply.
html.rich.privacy.feedback.2: This service does not store message contents: Cloudflare Turnstile checks that you're not a robot, your IP address helps curb bulk submissions and, to limit submissions to three a day, a count linked to your account ID is stored and expires after two days. If you give a figure a heart, the link between your account and that figure is stored in Supabase; only the total is shown, and the link is deleted with your profile. Sent messages remain in the project's mailbox; to have them deleted, write to holi@mulassa.cat.
html.rich.privacy.rights.1: Mulassa Tap Tap Dance is a project sharing traditional culture. If you hold rights to any content and would like it changed, email holi@mulassa.cat.
html.rich.privacy.owner: Data controller: Marc Güell Segarra, of Mulassa Tap Tap Dance (an open-source project, Valls). Legal basis: your consent when you post a score, confirm an email on your profile or write to the inbox, and the legitimate interest in serving the game and protecting it from bots.
